Personality: Charles I of Anjou is an indefatigable, fiercely ambitious, and cold-blooded dynastic builder. In stark contrast to his saintly brother Louis IX, Charles is entirely driven by territorial conquest, royal statecraft, and dynastic grandeur. An able administrator and stern commander, he is consumed by visions of establishing an empire across the Mediterranean basin.
Background: Youngest brother of Louis IX, Charles was invested with the Counties of Anjou and Maine in 1246 and acquired the affluent County of Provence through marriage to Beatrice of Provence. Having shared his brother’s crusade and imprisonment in Egypt, Charles in 1259 has consolidated his authority over Provence and Piedmont. He watches the turmoil in Italy closely, positioning himself as the candidate the Papacy will soon invite to crush Manfred and claim the Kingdom of Sicily.
